items.definition:
to negotiate again, especially to change the terms of an agreement
They decided to renegotiate the contract terms.

to make an aggressive growl with bared teeth
The dog began to snarl at the stranger.

to make a light, clear ringing sound
The small bell began to tink softly.

to make a groove, hole, or indentation with a sharp object
He accidentally gouged the wooden table with his knife.

to admit (someone) to a hospital for treatment
He had to be hospitalised after the accident.

to embed (something) in a surface or object
The craftsman will inlay mother-of-pearl into the wooden box.

to make someone feel sick or disgusted
The smell of the rotten food began to nauseate him.

to delay or postpone action; put off doing something
He tends to procrastinate when faced with difficult tasks.

to establish again
They hope to reestablish diplomatic relations.

to light or ignite again; to revive
They tried to rekindle their old friendship.

to place in a different position
We need to reposition the furniture in the living room.

to torment or tease (someone) with the sight or promise of something unobtainable
The smell of fresh bread tantalized him.

Make a series of low, feeble sounds expressive of fear, pain, or unhappiness.
The dog began to whimper during the thunderstorm.

wave or flourish (something, especially a weapon) as a threat or in anger or excitement
He brandished his sword at the enemy.

to spend the winter in a dormant state
Bears hibernate during the cold winter months.

to collapse inward violently
The old building was scheduled to implode safely.

to connect with one another
The various systems need to interconnect seamlessly.

To cut off (a branch, head, or limb) from the main body.
The gardener decided to lop off the dead branches from the tree.

to make something active again
You need to reactivate your account after a period of inactivity.

to smile or speak in a contemptuous or mocking manner
He couldn't help but sneer at their foolishness.

to make or become stable
The doctors worked to stabilise the patient's condition.

to secretly listen to telephone conversations
The police obtained a warrant to wiretap the suspect's phone.

to diminish or put at rest (fear, suspicion, or worry)
The doctor tried to allay her fears about the surgery.

to laugh in a loud, harsh way
The witches began to cackle as they stirred their cauldron.

to take advantage of; to write or print in capital letters
They hope to capitalise on the growing market for organic food.

to make inactive or ineffective
The enzyme was used to inactivate the virus.

to stare at in a lecherous or unpleasant way
It's rude to ogle people as they pass by.

treat with an apparent kindness that betrays a feeling of superiority
Please don't patronise me; I understand perfectly well.

argue or raise objections about a trivial matter
Let's not quibble over minor details.

remember (something)
I can't quite recollect where I put my keys.

go back over (a path or course)
We had to retrace our steps to find the lost wallet.

convert (a coded message) into intelligible language
The intelligence agency managed to decrypt the enemy's messages.

to take apart
He had to disassemble the furniture to move it.

to leave a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle
Passengers were asked to disembark the plane quickly.

play and move about cheerfully, excitedly, or energetically
The puppies loved to frolic in the grass.

act as a goalkeeper
He was chosen to goalkeep for the school team.

act as a goaltender
She learned to goaltend in her first year of ice hockey.

To equip with military resources; to give a military character to
The government decided to militarize the border region.

To prepare and organize for active service or use (British English spelling)
The community managed to mobilise quickly after the disaster.

to take the work or an idea of someone else and pass it off as one's own.
It is wrong to plagiarize someone else's essay.

to make something known to the public.
They hired a firm to publicise their new product.

to develop again or in a new way.
The city plans to redevelop the old industrial area.

to scold or criticize angrily
The coach would often berate his players for their mistakes.

extend the application of (a method or conclusion) to an unknown situation by assuming that existing trends will continue or similar methods will be applicable
We can extrapolate the results to the larger population.

add notes to (a melody) to produce harmony; make consistent or compatible
The singers tried to harmonize their voices.

to prevent something or someone from moving
The doctor had to immobilize her arm after the injury.

Defeat or get the better of (someone) by being more clever or cunning.
The mouse managed to outsmart the cat and escape.

To state again or in a different way.
Could you please restate your question?

conduct or carry out (business or financial dealings).
They transact business primarily online.

To make more urban in character.
The region has been rapidly urbanized over the last decade.

to approach and speak to (someone) often in an aggressive or unwanted way
The beggar would often accost passersby for money.

to warn or reprimand someone firmly
The teacher had to admonish the students for talking during the lesson.

to rebuke or reprimand severely
The coach had to chastise the player for his poor behavior.

to transfer power or authority from central to local government or administration
The company decided to decentralise its operations.

to discharge (waste matter) from the body or a tissue
The kidneys excrete waste products from the blood.

to convert into a fossil; to become rigid or old-fashioned
Over millions of years, the bones began to fossilize.

develop industries
Many countries sought to industrialise rapidly in the 19th century.

to avoid or neglect (a duty or responsibility)
He was accused of shirking his responsibilities.

to express excessive satisfaction or triumph
He couldn't help but gloat over his victory.

to dispute or bargain persistently, especially over the cost of something
She loves to haggle over prices at the market.

to begin a line of text further from the margin than the main part of the text
Please indent the first line of each paragraph.

to be far superior to
The champion boxer easily outclassed his opponent.

Cease to develop; become inactive or dull.
The economy began to stagnate after years of growth.

to make or become strong or resilient
The training will toughen the new recruits.
